t: Germany (1897) and Belgium (1916) ruled through the Tutsi king and treated Hutu and Tutsi as different races; Belgium's identity cards of 1935 fixed the labels, and the Hutu revolution of 1959 drove over 100,000 Tutsi into exile before independence on 1 July 1962.

Between 500,000 and 1,000,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were killed in about 100 days from 6 April 1994 in attacks planned and ordered by the interim government; the RPF's military victory in July ended the genocide.

Under the RPF and Paul Kagame, president since 2000, poverty fell from 60.3% in 2000 to 27.4% in 2024 and the economy grew 9.4% in 2025, while elections are manipulated and Human Rights Watch documents detention, disappearances and torture.
dyk: Rwanda joined the Commonwealth of Nations in 2009 as one of its few members with no historical link to the British Empire, and in 2008 it changed the medium of instruction in its schools from French to English.
ev: The Rwandan Revolution: Hutu activists kill Tutsi and burn their houses, driving more than 100,000 people into neighbouring countries.
On 1 July Rwanda, separated from Burundi after a 1961 referendum abolished the monarchy, becomes independent under President Grégoire Kayibanda.
Juvénal Habyarimana takes power in a military coup; pro-Hutu discrimination continues with less violence and more prosperity.
The Rwandan Patriotic Front, formed of Tutsi refugees, invades northern Rwanda from Uganda, beginning the Rwandan Civil War.
On 6 April Habyarimana's plane is shot down near Kigali; within hours the genocide begins, killing 500,000 to 1,000,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu in about 100 days.
The RPF takes control of the whole country, ending the genocide; some two million Hutu flee to Zaïre and other neighbours.
Paul Kagame, the RPF's former commander, becomes president; a constitution follows in 2003 after a national referendum.
On 25 January the Democratic Republic of the Congo severs diplomatic relations over Rwanda's support for the M23 rebellion after the Goma offensive.

f.founder: Grégoire Kayibanda, first president of the Hutu-dominated republic of 1962
f.predecessor: The Kingdom of Rwanda under the Tutsi Nyiginya kings; German East Africa (1897–1916); the Belgian mandate and trust territory of Ruanda-Urundi (1916–1962)
